proposed_fix.description: Confirm CPU saturation or throttling on recommendationservice, then, with approval, raise its CPU limit modestly and check whether a load or code change caused the jump.
steps: Check whether recommendationservice pods are being CPU-throttled (container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods) and compare CPU usage to current requests and limits.
Check for a recent deploy, config change or traffic increase on recommendationservice that matches the onset of the CPU and latency jump (E1, E2).
Check that CPU requests match actual usage, and adjust requests if they are clearly too low.
If throttling is confirmed and the service is erratic, raise the CPU limit on the recommendationservice container only (requests can stay the same), in a small increment, after human approval.
If CPU stays high after the limit increase, scale out replicas as a gated step, or roll back the recent change if one was found.
Watch recommendationservice CPU and latency p50/p90 and frontend latency after each change to confirm recovery.
preconditions: Throttling or CPU saturation is confirmed on recommendationservice pods, not only inferred from latency.
The node has spare CPU capacity and is not cordoned, so a higher limit or more replicas can be scheduled.
A recent deploy or traffic change has been checked, so a regression is not masked by adding CPU.
A human has approved each change.
proposed_fix.rollback: Restore the previous CPU limit/requests and replica count (for example by reverting the deployment manifest or running kubectl rollout undo), then confirm the metrics return to their pre-change values.

contradictions.step: The alert is purely informative and unless there is some other issue with the application, it can be skipped.
contradictions.why: CPU is up about 656% and latency is up 780-867% on recommendationservice, so there is another issue with the application and the alert cannot be skipped.
